name: Electric Objects EO1
notes: 23-inch wall-mount picture frame, abandoned by manufacturer. Linux-based, SSH access via stock firmware bug. Founder revived one in ~6h with Claude assistance.

name: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B
notes: Default tinkerer choice. Boring but always works. Use as baseline; recommend more interesting hardware first.

name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
notes: Smaller than Pi 4B, lower power. Good for projects that need to be embedded/hidden. Reasonable Wi-Fi. Slightly slow CPU but usually enough.

name: Tidbyt (Gen 1)
notes: 64x32 LED matrix, ESP32-based. Community firmware (Tronbyt) supports self-hosted apps without Tidbyt cloud.

name: Barnes & Noble Nook Simple Touch (BNRV300)
notes: 2011 e-reader, Android 2.1 underneath. Well-documented root via SD card. Used widely as wall-mounted dashboard / status display.

name: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (Gen 2, 2013)
notes: Older Kindles (PW2 era) jailbreak via known firmware paths. Used widely as low-power dashboard / calendar / weather displays. KOReader runs custom apps.

name: Kobo Clara HD
notes: 6-inch e-ink reader, Linux underneath. Telnet/SSH via 'developer mode' file. KOReader and InkBox provide custom OSes. More open than Kindle.

name: Apple iPad 2
notes: Dirt-cheap on eBay. Guided Access locks it to a single app for kiosk use. No jailbreak required for calendar/dashboard. Older models can run iOS 9.x.

name: Philips Hue Go (1st gen)
notes: Portable Hue lamp with battery. Pairs with Zigbee2MQTT or Home Assistant. Programmable color animations are the killer use case for ambient/breathing apps.

name: ESP32 DevKit-C
notes: Default ESP32 board for tinkering. Wi-Fi + BLE, runs MicroPython or Arduino. Common in DIY ambient displays, sensor relays, custom IoT projects.

name: Olimex ESP32-POE
notes: ESP32 with PoE Ethernet. Single cable for power and network — good for wall-mounted displays/sensors with no wall-warts.

name: TP-Link TL-WR841N (router)
notes: Cheap consumer router. OpenWrt support varies by hardware revision (v8+ are constrained). Listed for projects needing a tiny Linux box with Wi-Fi where Pi is overkill.

name: Wyze Cam v2
notes: $25 cloud camera. Custom firmware (openmiko) gives RTSP and frees from Wyze cloud. Good for home automation streams; the older v2 is the documented target.

name: Pebble Time (smartwatch)
notes: Discontinued e-paper smartwatch. Rebble.io keeps it alive with free app store and custom watchfaces. Cheap on eBay; week-long battery; SDK still works.

name: Google Chromecast (1st gen, H2G2-42)
notes: $5-15 on eBay. Original Chromecast (not Ultra/Audio). Linux-based; community 'eureka-rom' projects exist for full control. HDMI output for an ambient TV display.

name: Dell Wyse 5070 (thin client)
notes: x86 thin client (Pentium Silver, 4GB RAM, fanless). $40-80 on eBay. Boots any Linux distro from USB. Better than a Pi for desktop-grade workloads, low power.

name: HP t620 Plus (thin client)
notes: AMD GX-420CA, dual NIC, 4 USB. $30-60. Popular as a tiny pfSense/OPNsense firewall, Pi-hole box, or home server. Common in homelab community.

name: Nintendo 3DS
notes: Massive modding scene. CFW (Luma3DS) enables homebrew, emulators, region-free play. Brick risk REAL on bad installs — the 3ds.hacks.guide walkthrough is the canonical source.

name: Atari Flashback (HDMI plug-and-play)
notes: Retro-styled mini-console. Hacking is non-trivial. Llm-inferred + handheld = brick-risk score will be stripped from output by safety rule.

name: Arduino Uno R3
notes: The classic. Not Wi-Fi, not powerful, but trivially programmable for sensors, motor control, blinkenlights. First step before ESP32 for many tinkerers.

name: Waveshare 7.5" e-Paper HAT (V2)
notes: 800x480 mono e-paper, drives off Pi Zero W via SPI. THE canonical kitchen-calendar build (MagInkCal, InkyPi). Refresh ~2-5s; perfect for static daily layouts. Pair with Pi Zero W for the classic combo.

name: Waveshare 10.3" e-Paper (HD, parallel/SPI)
notes: 1872x1404 mono e-ink. Larger than 7.5" so suits a kitchen wall calendar or magazine-style display. Needs IT8951 driver board. More expensive (~$200+) but gorgeous.

name: Pimoroni Inky Impression 7.3" (7-color)
notes: 800x480 SEVEN-COLOR e-paper HAT. 7-color e-ink is rare — great for ambient art rotation, family photos, weather displays. Slow refresh (~30s) so static-frame use only. Pi Zero W compatible.

name: reMarkable 2 (e-paper tablet)
notes: 10.3" mono e-paper with stylus. Linux underneath. Toltec package manager + Oxide launcher = full custom OS. Premium ($300+) but a polished tinkerer device. Expensive failure mode if bricked.

name: Pimoroni HyperPixel 4.0 (Pi LCD)
notes: 4-inch high-PPI IPS LCD that mounts directly on a Pi (no HDMI cable). Great for self-contained dashboards, smart-home controllers, pi-in-a-box projects. Touch variant available.

name: LILYGO TTGO T5 V2.3 (ESP32 + 2.13" e-Paper)
notes: All-in-one ESP32 + 2.13" e-paper. Tiny, battery-friendly, $20-30. Perfect for badge displays, weather stations, status indicators. Larger 4.7" T5 variant exists for bigger projects.

name: Boox Poke 3 (Android e-reader)
notes: 6" e-ink with stock Android 10 + Google Play. Sideload any Android app — Google Calendar, custom dashboards, kiosk launchers. Less hacking required than a Kindle/Kobo because it's already open.
